orientation.notes: Only own prop besides the shared className/style/render.

className/style/render.type: string | fn / CSSProperties | fn / ReactElement | fn

renderProp.elementForm: render={<hr />} or any element (default is a <div>)

keyboard.keys: None — role="separator" is not focusable by default.
keyboard.focus: None; add tabIndex on the rendered element if an interactive separator is ever needed.

notableDifferences: React Aria's Separator exposes orientation only as well, so this is a near 1:1 swap; the differences are the props name (identical) and the output (role="separator" + aria-orientation emitted by Base UI).
Base UI renders a <div> by default (React Aria renders an <hr> by default), so existing CSS selectors/tag assumptions may need updating — pass render={<hr />} to keep the old markup.
State is a single data-orientation attribute; there is no data-disabled since Separator cannot be disabled.
OTPField re-exports this same Separator, so <OTPField.Separator> is the same component with the same behaviour.
